incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (CO 2014), ss. 5, 6, 17–19; Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010 section 7(1)(k) exempt-company status; Financial Services (Distributed Ledger Technology Providers) Regulations 2018 for licensed DLT activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies House, Government of Gibraltar, Suite 964, Europort, Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation and Memorandum & Articles of Association (Form CO-AC-CAR), filed with attached Declaration of Compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The exempted company is a non-profit company limited by guarantee with zero share capital. No paid-up capital is required, no escrow account deposit is mandated, and the members' guarantee is stated in the memorandum (typically GBP 1 or equivalent per member, payable only on winding-up).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that: (1) The Company is incorporated as an exempted company under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 and adopts the Memorandum and Articles of Association tabled before the Board. (2) The Directors ratify the allotment and issue of one non-voting management share of no par value to the Founding Member for administrative convenience, with no payment required. (3) The registered office of the Company shall be at the address provided by the formation agent, and such address is hereby approved. (4) The Directors shall promptly appoint the first Company Secretary, registered agent, and any required compliance officer. (5) The Board shall engage the external legal counsel to submit the taxation exemption certification and any applicable DLT licensing application to the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the Companies House e-Registry, specifying the proposed entity name and confirming that the name contains a limited-liability or foundation indicator in compliance with the Companies Act. Reserve the name for 30 days and obtain the name-clearance receipt to use in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (with 'Limited by Guarantee' or 'Foundation' suffix as appropriate)
Brief statement of non-profit object (open-source protocol governance)
Identification details of the founding member and prospective director
Confirmatory search results from the Gibraltar corporate register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as existing or misleading, re-submit with an alternative name and, if necessary, request a formal written review from the Registry within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies House
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CO-AC-CAR together with the electronic Memorandum and Articles of Association, execute all statutory declarations and consent-to-act forms, attach the name-reservation receipt, and pay the incorporation fee. Filing is performed online; if paper filing is used, same-day courier of notarized originals is required. The Certificate of Incorporation will be issued upon verification.
required_dossiers: Form CO-AC-CAR
Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed by incorporator)
Declaration of Compliance (Form CO-6)
Consent to Act as Director forms
Proof of registered office address in Gibraltar
Identity and verification documents for all directors and the secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a query, respond formally within 14 days through the Companies House Portal, amend the submitted documents if required, and request expedited re-review. If the Registry rejects the filing, appeal to the Registry's internal adjudication unit and file a fresh submission with the Registry's objections addressed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Company Secretary Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House and the Company Secretary (licensed corporate service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, execute a registered office service agreement with a local Gibraltar licensed service provider, file a registered office address notice with the Registry, and formally appoint a qualified company secretary. Ensure that the registered office is a physical address in Gibraltar and is open during statutory hours.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office address consent letter from landlord/provider
Appointment letter for company secretary
Signed declaration of acceptance by the secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office or secretary appointment is rejected for non-licensing of the service provider, replace the provider with a fully licensed trust company and re-file the notice within 7 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Statutory Governance Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, Company Secretary, and notary/public official if physical meeting held
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (in person, by telephone, or by video-call under the Companies Act). Approve the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer designation as set out in the pro-forma resolution. Record minutes and issue an extract signed by the chair.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Drafted minutes of the first board meeting
Share register and members' guarantee ledger (if any)
Director consents and notices of residential address (or service address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer appointment is invalid due to non-consent or conflict, cure by obtaining ratified written consent retroactively or by fresh appointment at an adjourned board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption Certification and DLT Licensing Pre-screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: HM Minister for Constitution and Financial Services (for exemption certificate) and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) (for DLT licensing or registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Government for an exempted-company tax status certificate under the Income Tax Act, declaring non-resident and non-trade-in-Gibraltar status. Simultaneously, if the foundation will perform any regulated DLT activity (including operating a public protocol as a business), file for the provisional DLT Provider Authorisation with GFSC; for pure non-profit foundational oversight with no custody or exchange activity, file the required notice for a statutory exemption or obtain confirmation of non-licensability.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum & Articles of Association
Board resolution seeking tax and DLT licensing status
Audited undeclared low-revenue certificate or representation letter (for exemption)
Policies on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing
Business plan describing the protocol-governance non-profit activity
Identity and reputational documentation of the ultimate beneficial owner and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the exemption certificate is refused, re-emphasize the non-lucrative nature and lack of local trading nexus, or restructure to a pure association; if GFSC refuses DLT authorization, appeal to the GFSC Review Committee and take corrective measures to satisfy the regulatory perimeter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) – DLT Supervisory Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Distributed Ledger Technology Provider Licence or Limited Licence (Financial Services (Distributed Ledger Technology Providers) Regulations 2018)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Agency, HM Government of Gibraltar – Department of the Environment, Sustainability, Heritage and Climate Change
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Environmental Impact Registration (low-impact office-only use; no full EIA mandated unless physical infrastructure is installed).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater must comply with the Gibraltar Water Act 2015 municipal sewer discharge standards (BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L). No VOC emissions from non-industrial office activities; all electronic waste must be disposed of under the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (Gibraltar) Regulations 2011, and any backup generator emissions must comply with the local Clean Air (Emission of Gaseous Pollutants) Regulations 2021.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service under the Fire (Safety in Public Places) Act 1996; structural stability inspection certificate issued by a licensed local engineer from the Buildings Department; permanent premises must have a valid public liability insurance and a written Occupational Safety and Health risk assessment approved by the Health & Safety Authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office (ITO); portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company seeking a Gibraltar tax nexus must first be registered as a foreign company under the Gibraltar Companies Act or otherwise maintain a registered office in Gibraltar. The Income Tax Office issues a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) upon submission of Form CT1 (non-resident/foreign entity registration), certified copy of the Bermuda certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, constitutional documents, proof of registered office in Gibraltar, and AML/KYC files of the ultimate beneficial owners. The application is processed after verification of economic substance and physical presence indicators required under the Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). If the entity has no permanent establishment or taxable Gibraltar-source activity, a TRN may still be required for nil-return filing or for Purchase Tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Election for exempt status under the Income Tax Act for non-resident companies; election to be treated as a territorial-scope company for non-Gibraltar-source income; and the applicable economic substance elections mandated by the Gibraltar ESR. Hybrid mismatch elections under Gibraltar's controlled foreign company and territorial tax rules are not generally available to exempted companies but may be considered by election for financing structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold; any person importing or exporting chargeable goods into or out of Gibraltar is required to register with the Gibraltar Customs and Excise Department and obtain a Purchase Tax registration number. Registration is mandatory regardless of turnover if the person carries on a taxable import/export business or makes taxable purchases of restricted goods (GIP).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar does not operate a real-time national e-invoicing or fiscal clearance system for Purchase Tax. Import declarations must be lodged electronically via the ASYCUDA World customs management system. Digital stamping or authenticated electronic invoices are not currently imposed. For supply-chain transparency in the Web3 context, the customs clearance platform requires electronic filing of import/export declarations, commodity codes, valuation data, and origin documentation; approval is granted through system-generated Customs Entry Numbers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of Purchase Tax applies to the physical export of goods from Gibraltar to a destination outside Gibraltar, provided the goods are exported within a prescribed period (generally within 12 weeks of purchase) and are not consumed in Gibraltar. For digital services, Web3 foundation protocol services are outside the scope of Gibraltar Purchase Tax because Purchase Tax only applies to goods brought into Gibraltar; offshore services supplied to non-Gibraltar persons do not attract the tax. Claims for zero-rated export treatment require proof of physical removal from Gibraltar, the exporter's Purchase Tax registration, and retention of compliant evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (ENS via ASYCUDA World)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill showing Gibraltar as departure point and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank remittance evidence demonstrating consideration received from outside Gibraltar
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HM Government of Gibraltar – Customs and Excise may audit export claims within six years. A false zero-rating claim or failure to substantiate export within the required deadline results in clawback of the Purchase Tax previously relieved, plus interest. Penalties range from 50% to 300% of the tax evaded, with contempt-type fines, forfeiture of goods, and criminal liability for officers of the entity. For Web3 entities, fraudulent offshore service or export declarations can also trigger suspension of the Gibraltar TRN and referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar through the Commissioner of Currency issues the Gibraltar pound; the Bank of England is the sovereign monetary authority and lender of last resort; the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the conduct, AML/CFT and foreign-exchange supervision authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory with no independent central bank and no exchange-control statute. The Gibraltar pound is fully backed by and convertible at par with pound sterling. Both capital-account and current-account movements are free from exchange-control approval; profit, grant, dividend, licensing and token-treasury remittances may be repatriated without surrender or conversion obligations. Practical convertibility constraints arise from correspondent-bank de-risking, GFSC anti-money-laundering due-diligence and sanctions screening rather than from statutory currency controls. A Bermuda Exempted Company using Gibraltar as its treasury venue should maintain a board-approved currency policy and evidence of source of funds for all conversions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender period and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in Gibraltar. Export proceeds, service fees, grant receipts and digital-asset proceeds may be retained in the original receipt currency, held in USDC or converted at the entity's commercial discretion in GIP, GBP, EUR or USD. For evidential compliance, the treasury should maintain a foreign-currency receipts ledger matching each invoice, grant agreement or smart-contract transaction with bank statements and, where applicable, an on-chain audit trail.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium as a primary banking rail. Gibraltar has a GFSC-administered electronic-money framework under the Financial Services Act, but most offshore digital EMI providers are not authorised in Gibraltar and post-Brexit passporting from the UK or EEA does not extend to Gibraltar. Mainstream EMIs generally classify token foundations as prohibited or high-risk and reject non-profit Web3 entities. A more viable substitute is a GFSC-licensed DLT provider or an authorised investment-firm custody arrangement holding segregated funds, with commercial banking at a tier-1 Gibraltar bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar law does not absolutely require physical attendance if the bank applies equivalent enhanced due diligence, but for a Web3 foundation with a Bermuda Exempted Company structure the practical standard is a physical or high-definition video identity interview for every director and beneficial owner. At least one director or a Gibraltar-resident company secretary/fiduciary must normally attend the interview at the bank's Gibraltar premises or before an approved notary. Fully remote opening without a professional introducer is not administratively available for this business profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Token foundation purpose and receipts from unregulated digital-asset exchanges
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion classifying the governance token as a utility or non-security asset; whitepaper; smart-contract security audit; token-generation event terms; wallet-address inventory showing no unbacked exchange inflows; travel-rule and transaction-monitoring policy; GFSC-compliant AML/CFT programme for the foundation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity in a Bermuda Exempted Company with nominee shareholder arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Registrar certificate; certificate of incorporation; memorandum and articles; register of members; declaration of trust over shares; evidence that no bearer shares exist; full passport, residential address, nationality and source-of-wealth for every natural person owning or controlling more than 10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-profit governance mismatch and unregulated cross-border grant disbursements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation deed or charitable-equivalent status certificate; governance charter; grant-committee minutes; annual budget and treasury policy; approved disbursement matrix; audited or board-reviewed financial statements; KYC and AML file for each grantee and vendor including legal name, country, and wallet address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent-bank de-risking due to stablecoin and cross-border crypto exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent risk assessment prepared by a Gibraltar-licensed DLT or financial-services adviser; continuous transaction monitoring with native-USDC tracing; OFAC, EU and UN sanctions screening; proof that no mixing services, privacy wallets or sanctioned addresses touched the treasury; negative-news and adverse-media report; professional indemnity or crime policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound treasury injections should be routed over SWIFT MT103 for USD and, where available, via CHAPS or SEPA for GBP and EUR into the Bermuda Exempted Company's dedicated Gibraltar operating account or a segregated capital escrow account. The remittance narrative must state the true purpose, for example 'equity capital injection', 'founder loan' or 'grant for open-source protocol development', and the remitting bank must map that narrative to the applicable balance-of-payments purpose code used by the sending jurisdiction. For a capital contribution the correct category is a capital-account code, not a services-code. Verification must include the SWIFT ACK or MT199 acknowledgement, the bank credit advice, a matching board-approved capital budget entry, and confirmation that the inflow has been included in the entity's accounting and AML source-of-funds file. Stablecoin or token injections should first be liquidated by a regulated counterparty and then moved by fiat wire; direct exchange-wallet transfers to the main operating account should be avoided unless supported by a complete transaction-level audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Fiat disbursements for grants, development services, legal fees, accounting fees and operational suppliers are cleared through SWIFT MT103 with the payee's full legal name, bank identifier and invoice reference embedded in the remittance field. If physical goods, hardware procurement or documentary services are involved, a commercial letter of credit may be opened under the foundation's banking facility, supported by the underlying commercial invoice, packing list and shipping documents. For final settlement involving the foundation's Web3 treasury, disbursements should be executed as native USDC transfers from a Gnosis Safe multisig vault with a pre-specified signer quorum, on-chain remittance metadata, and the same invoice or grant-agreement reference. No outbound instruction, whether fiat or stablecoin, may be released without a positive sanctions-screen, beneficiary KYC check and dual-authorisation within the board-approved treasury policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts in GIP, GBP, EUR and USD with tenors up to 24 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with an authorised Gibraltar or UK bank or broker.
FX swap transactions converting stablecoin-denominated treasury receipts into operating currencies on a spot-and-forward basis.
Cross-currency swaps matching the foundation's USDC-native assets against GBP or EUR operating liabilities, limited to treasury hedging and prohibited for speculative open positions.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for illiquid or non-convertible currencies where physical delivery is legally impossible, with settlement in USDC, GBP or EUR and no physical exchange.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return and Authorised Share Capital Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Financial Services Commission, Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of incorporation; payment due within 30 days after the anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts statutory penalties of 10% per month; failure for 6 months may cause administrative strike-off and loss of exempted status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registration Office, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of registration of the overseas company in Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of £30; continued default beyond 3 months triggers formal warning; more than 6 months leads to removal from the Gibraltar registry and possible personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Central Beneficial Ownership Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the company's annual return date and promptly upon any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal offence with fines up to £5,000 per officer and £2,500 for the company; continuing default may lead to strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Company Tax Return / Non-Profit Nil Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months from the end of the accounting period (typically 31 December for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty of £100 and daily default penalties of £60/day; assessments may be raised on an estimated basis.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Financial Statements and Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Every director liable to a fine up to £2,000; persistent default may lead to disqualification proceedings and strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Gibraltar-registered entity engaged in DLT/token foundation activities is subject to mandatory audit as a public-interest/regulated entity. Other companies must undergo audit unless they qualify as small under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014: turnover not exceeding £10.2 million, balance sheet not exceeding £5.1 million, and not more than 50 employees; small company exemption is lost if members holding at least 10% request audit or the entity is a public-interest subsidiary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as applied in Gibraltar (UK-adopted IFRS equivalents); IFRS for SMEs is available for qualifying small entities. For the Bermuda exempted company, accounts may be prepared under Bermuda Financial Reporting Framework (aligned with IFRS).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Gibraltar: maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and file an annual confirmation statement with the central registry within 14 days after the annual return date; any transfer of a beneficial shareholding must be updated both internally and centrally before the next confirmation. Bermuda: the exempted company must make an annual resolution confirming register accuracy and record share transfers; the confirmation accompanies the annual government fee filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Company Secretary

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,200 – $3,500 standard Gibraltar registered office/agent/UBO service; Bermuda registered office and local secretary add $2,000 – $6,000 if separately maintained
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $15,000 – $50,000 for a specialised digital asset/non-profit foundation audit under IFRS

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010 ('ITA 2010') standard corporate rate 12.5% (FY 2021 onwards; prior effective 10%). A Bermuda Exempted Company whose central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar is Gibraltar tax resident and chargeable on worldwide income; the Bermuda exempt status confers no Gibraltar relief. Non-profit pathway: ITA 2010 s.46 grants full exemption for a body established exclusively for charitable purposes where the income is applied solely to those objects and the Commissioner of Income Tax has granted exemption — the Web3 Foundation (ISIC 6499, non-profit token foundation) should file an exemption application for donation/token-grant income applied to open-source Layer-1/2 protocol governance and R&D. Additional effective-rate reductions: super-deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure, and the 0% withholding regime on qualifying EU/EEA interest and royalties. No preferential IP box or patent box exists in Gibraltar.
